title: Demand-slope autoscaler and soft-reservation warmup
author: Anika Bose
release_notes: Introduces a demand-slope-based autoscaler with soft reservation warmup. Improves P99 latency stability during sudden demand ramps and reduces cold-start provisioning by proactively seeding warm capacity. Config knobs added under dedicated.autoscaler.slope_window and dedicated.reservation.warmup_fraction.
description:
Motivation: Frequent short-lived ramps (bursty customer workloads) were causing either overprovisioning or reactive autoscaling-induced latency spikes. Existing moving-average based autoscalers are slow to react to steep demand slopes and aggressive step-scaling leads to oscillation. This PR implements a demand-slope autoscaler that: 1) measures demand slope (requests/minute delta over short windows), 2) translates steep positive slope into proactive warmup reservations using a leaky-bucket decay model, and 3) exposes soft-reservation semantics that can be preempted gracefully under sustained pressure. Key behavioral goals: reduce P99 inflation on sudden ramps, avoid long warmup churn, and keep sustained cost overhead low.

High-level design: The autoscaler observes per-tenant request rate and slot utilization. It computes a demand_slope = linear_regression_slope(window=30s) and a confidence score (variance-normalized). If demand_slope exceeds threshold, the planner allocates soft_warm_units = min(max_warm, ceil(k * demand_slope)). Soft reservations are recorded in the reservation ledger with a decay token that follows a leaky-bucket: each warm token ages and decays at rate lambda; the allocator treats soft tokens as low-priority slots that can be reclaimed with a short preemption window (configurable). The mechanism is pluggable into existing Dedicated provisioning loop and prioritizes tenant-level fairness via a normalized urgency score.

Config and API changes: - config.dedicated.autoscaler.slope_window_seconds (default 30) - config.dedicated.autoscaler.slope_threshold (default 5 rps/s) - config.dedicated.reservation.warmup_fraction (default 0.15) - config.dedicated.reservation.decay_lambda (default 0.08) - New metrics prefix: dedicated.autoscaler.slope.*, dedicated.reservation.soft_* - Exposed small admin endpoint: POST /admin/reservations/preview (dry-run) for SRE diagnostics

Performance results (internal perf-canary): - Synthetic ramp test (x10 in 8s): baseline P99 increased +220ms; this branch P99 increased +50ms. - Sustained plateau tests: added cost overhead ~3.4% on short ramps, negligible (<0.5%) steady-state. - Canary observed reduced thrash events on allocator logs (reduced rebind rate by ~38%).

Commits (summary): - feat(autoscaler): add slope estimator and demand scoring (3 commits) - feat(reservations): introduce soft reservation ledger and decay algorithm (2 commits) - refactor(provisioner): plumb warmup path into dedicated provision loop (1 commit) - observability: add slope and reservation metrics, dashboard templates (1 commit) - tests: unit/integration for slope logic and preemption path (2 commits)

Files changed (high level): - services/dedicated/autoscaler/slope_estimator.go (new) - services/dedicated/autoscaler/planner.go (modified) - services/dedicated/reservation/soft_ledger.go (new) - services/dedicated/provisioner/warmup_integration.go (modified) - docs/ops/autoscaler-warmup.md (new) - observability/dashboards/dedicated_autoscaler.json (new) - tests/dedicated/autoscaler_slope_test.go (new) - api/admin/reservation_preview.go (new) - config/defaults/dedicated.yaml (modified)

Review conversation (summary, single-threaded): - Marco Chen (reviewer): "Nice approach. A couple of questions on safety: what happens if many tenants all ramp at once? We should ensure soft reservations don't starve guaranteed allocations." - Anika (author): "We bound warmup by tenant_fraction_of_pool and global_warm_cap; soft reservations are preemptable and accounted separately from hard reservations. Added explicit tests for global contention scenario." - Elena Martinez: "Can you add an integration test that simulates interleaved microbursts from 50 tenants? Also please include dashboard runbook steps for ops." - Anika: "Added integration harness and dashboard/ops doc; expanded metrics with the 'reclaimed_soft_tokens' counter so SRE can detect heavy preemption." - Jonah Li: "LGTM after addressing minor naming nit and CI flake fix." - Jonah provided an approval: "APPROVED by Jonah Li on 2026-01-25"

CI and validation: - CI matrix: unit (go test), integration (small harness), lint (staticcheck), build (docker images). - Initial CI failed on flaky allocator test (race on ledger update). Fixed by adding ledger CAS and a retry backoff. - Final CI status: all checks passed on run #5.

Ops rollout plan: - Dry-run (canary) in us-west-2 Dedicated pool with warmup_fraction=0.10 for 48h - Monitor dedicated.autoscaler.slope.p99, dedicated.reservation.soft_reclaimed_rate, and provisioner.rebind_rate - If no regressions, gradually enable in other pools and raise warmup_fraction to 0.15

Backward compatibility and safety: - All configs have sensible defaults; feature is disabled for tenants without dedicated pools. - Soft reservations are non-binding and will not count toward billing. - Added toggles behind config.dedicated.autoscaler.enable_slope_autoscaler for quick rollback.

Merge: Squash-and-merge performed by Elena Martinez on 2026-01-26. Cherry-pick notes: none. Follow-ups: ENG-2618 (tune warmup_fraction per workload), ENG-2699 (extend slope estimator to include sequence-length weighted demand).
notes: Hotfix follow-up: after merging we observed a single customer with extremely bursty traffic generating >20x slope. Ops temporarily set warmup_fraction to 0.05 for that tenant while we tune per-tenant caps. Tracking in SUP-4321.
